panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a real patient clinical photo captioned as fringe sign, defined in-text as retention of hairs along frontal or temporal rim, highly suggestive of traction alopecia, with visible marginal alopecia. B: Panel B is a real patient clinical photo captioned as tenting, defined in-text as raising of skin on scalp when hair is pulled extremely tightly, important exam finding for diagnosing traction alopecia, with visible marginal thinning under tight braids; tenting not in vocabulary so retained as proposed finding.

Fringe sign is the retention of hairs along the frontal or temporal rim (Figure 6A). Highly suggestive of excessive tension, tenting of hair follicles refers to the raising of skin on the scalp when hair is pulled extremely tightly (Figure 6B). Both are important exam findings for diagnosing traction alopecia (67, 68).
